mainTopic: Does שבת, תרומה, or a person's designation fix produce for מעשרות? The view of רבי אליעזר, and רבי יוחנן's rule that only fruit whose work is finished becomes fixed.
overview: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר really holds that designating fruit for שבת fixes it for מעשרות. After all, the leftovers can go back to the pile, and in the משנה of olives from a vat he says returnable leftovers are not fixed. An attempt to explain the case as a pure storage area with an impure person is rejected, because the rest of the fruit never moved. Instead, רב שימי בר אשי says רבי אליעזר follows his own view: even taking תרומה fixes produce, and שבת all the more so. The גמרא then tries to prove from the חכמים that שבת fixes produce. That proof is rejected, because the person's own words 'from here to there' fixed the fruit, and the mention of שבת teaches that טבל counts as prepared for שבת. A ברייתא about finishing a cluster of grapes seems to contradict רבי אליעזר. רבי נתן explains that 'he may finish' means only after leaving the חצר or after שבת ends. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that שבת, תרומה, חצר and a purchase fix fruit only once its work is finished. Listing שבת rejects הלל, who forbids such fruit even before its work is done.

steps.title: But the leftovers go back, so how is anything fixed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the extra fruit can be returned, and רבי אליעזר holds that wherever leftovers return, nothing becomes fixed for מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the leftover goes back! And we know that רבי אליעזר said: wherever the leftover goes back, it does not become fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that setting fruit aside for later makes it fixed for מעשרות. It points to a rule of רבי אליעזר that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who designates fruit to eat later does not really commit to all of it, because whatever he does not eat can go back to the pile. רבי אליעזר himself holds that when the leftovers can be returned, there is no קביעה. So how can designating the fruit create קביעה?

keyTerms.meaning: Its leftover, the extra amount not eaten
Goes back, is returned
Fixed: the point where produce becomes forbidden to eat without separating מעשר
And we have heard from him, meaning we know this is his opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'fixed' (קבע) does not mean repaired. It is the technical point at which produce must be tithed before even a snack is allowed.

phrases.english: But isn't it so that its leftover goes back,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the fruit he set aside for later.

phrases.english: and we have heard that Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמוֹתָרוֹ חוֹזֵר — לָא קָבַע!
phrases.english: Anywhere that its leftover goes back, it does not become fixed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim on the daf that רבי אליעזר's designation fixes the fruit for מעשרות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that designating fruit for later creates קביעה for מעשרות according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leftovers can return to the pile, and רבי אליעזר rules that returnable leftovers prevent קביעה. Designation should therefore not fix anything.

steps.title: Source: the משנה of olives taken from a vat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה in which רבי אליעזר exempts olives from an impure vat because the person returns the surplus.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone who takes olives from the vat may dip them one at a time in salt and eat them. If he dipped and put ten in front of himself, he must tithe. רבי אליעזר says: from a pure vat he must tithe, from an impure vat he is exempt, because he puts the extra back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי אליעזר holds the rule quoted in step 1. It quotes a משנה where he gives exactly that reason: 'because he returns the surplus.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating olives one by one is only snacking, so no מעשר is needed. Gathering ten in front of yourself counts as a fixed meal, and the תנא קמא requires tithing. רבי אליעזר splits the case by the vat's purity, and his stated reason for exempting the impure vat is that the leftovers go back.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A vat where olives sit and soften before pressing
Dips
Obligated (to tithe first) / exempt (may snack without tithing)
Ritually pure / ritually impure

phrases.english: As we learned: One who takes olives from the vat
may dip them one by one in salt and eat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם טָבַל וְנָתַן לְפָנָיו עֲשָׂרָה — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: And if he dipped and placed ten before him, he is obligated.
phrases.notes: He has to separate מעשר before eating, since ten olives in front of him counts as a real meal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From a pure vat, he is obligated;
from an impure vat, he is exempt,
because he returns the surplus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rule of רבי אליעזר cited in the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds returnable leftovers prevent קביעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about olives from the מעטן, where רבי אליעזר exempts the case 'because he returns the surplus.'

steps.title: Why does purity make a difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier question: what is the difference between the pure-vat case and the impure-vat case?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: what is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls a question it once asked on this משנה. Why should the vat's purity change the law of מעשר? This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purity and tithing look like unrelated subjects. The question forces us to find how purity connects to whether the leftovers can go back. That connection is what makes the משנה a proof for step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it / raised a difficulty about it
What is different?
The first clause / the last clause

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא?
phrases.english: What is different in the first clause, and what is different in the last clause?
phrases.notes: The first clause is רבי אליעזר's pure-vat case, and the last clause is his impure-vat case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the purity of the vat affects the obligation to tithe.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: it depends on whether he can put the olives back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that in the pure vat an impure person cannot return the olives, so they are fixed. In the impure vat he can return them, so they are not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: the first case is a pure vat and an impure person, who cannot put the olives back. The last case is an impure vat and an impure person, who can put them back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question from step 3. The real issue is whether the leftover olives can go back into the vat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure person who touches the olives makes them impure. If the vat is pure, he cannot put them back without spoiling the rest, so what he takes is truly his and it is fixed. If the vat is already impure, returning them causes no harm, so he has not committed to them and they are not fixed. This confirms that רבי אליעזר holds returnable leftovers prevent קביעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The man, the person
Is able, can
Return it, put it back

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, if the leftovers can go back to the pile, taking food does not fix it for מעשרות. This is the basis for the challenge in step 1.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the purity detail into proof of a general principle of רבי אליעזר. That principle is what threatens the earlier claim that designating fruit fixes it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:
The first clause is about a pure vat and an impure man,
who cannot return it.
phrases.notes: He has made the olives impure by touching them, so putting them back would make the whole pure vat impure.

phrases.english: The last clause is about an impure vat and an impure man,
who can return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: רֵישָׁא בְּמַעֲטָן טָהוֹר וְגַבְרָא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3, which completes the proof for the challenge in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Purity matters only because it decides whether the leftovers can be returned. If they can be returned, there is no קביעה.

steps.title: The משנה is also a pure storage area with an impure person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies רבי אבהו's distinction to the משנה. It suggests that the משנה is a case of a pure storage area and an impure person, who cannot return the leftover fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is also talking about a pure storage area and an impure person, who cannot put the fruit back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי אבהו's answer to defend the משנה. Here the person cannot return the extra fruit, so the fruit can become fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 1 was that the leftovers can be returned, and רבי אליעזר holds that nothing is fixed when leftovers can return. The answer is that here they cannot return, because an impure person may not put fruit back into a pure storage area. So the 'return' rule does not apply, and the fixing stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a storage area where fruit is set aside to dry (not the usual שבת meaning)
Ritually pure
A ritually impure person
To return or put back

phrases.english: Our משנה too is about a pure storage area
and an impure person,
who cannot put it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי בְּמוּקְצֶה טָהוֹר וְגַבְרָא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אבהו's pure/impure distinction to the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leftover fruit could be returned, so nothing should be fixed
steps.terutzMaskana: The person is impure and the storage area is pure, so he cannot return the fruit, and it is fixed

steps.title: But the fruit is already in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer. The rest of the fruit never left the storage area, so there is nothing to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the fruits are already sitting in their place, as if returned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer it just gave. In the משנה the person only takes the portion he set aside, and everything else stays where it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pure/impure distinction only matters when someone takes fruit out and then puts back the extra. Here the rest of the fruit never left its place. So whether the person can return fruit is not the issue, and the answer does not fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Already standing in place, as if returned
But isn't it so...? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But aren't they already standing returned!
phrases.notes: He only takes the part he marked off. The rest never moved, so there is nothing to bring back.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is a pure-storage, impure-person case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Returning fruit is irrelevant when the leftover fruit never left its place

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי gives a new answer. רבי אליעזר holds that even separating תרומה fixes produce, so שבת certainly does. The משנה therefore reflects only his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב שימי בר אשי said: Are you quoting רבי אליעזר? רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning. He said that תרומה fixes produce, and שבת all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answer and offers a new one. רבי אליעזר's ruling comes from his own special opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that taking off תרומה fixes the produce even before its work is finished, and שבת is an even stronger reason to fix it. So of course, in his view, שבת fixes produce. But this only shows רבי אליעזר's opinion, so it does not settle the question for the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
The first portion given to a כהן
Fixes the produce, so it must be tithed before eating
All the more so

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the direction of the סוגיא. רב שימי בר אשי confirms that for רבי אליעזר, שבת does fix produce. But רבי אליעזר holds this as part of a minority view that the חכמים reject, so the גמרא now looks for a proof from the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
Are you quoting Rabbi Eliezer?
Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning, for he said:
Teruma fixes produce, and all the more so Shabbat.
phrases.notes: 'Fixes' means the produce now counts as ready, so you can't even snack on it until it's tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's ruling needs a special case to explain it
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds that even תרומה fixes produce, so for him שבת does too

steps.title: Source: רבי אליעזר says תרומה fixes produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. For fruit whose תרומה was taken before its work was finished, רבי אליעזר forbids even casual eating, while the חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Fruit from which תרומה was taken before its work was finished: רבי אליעזר forbids eating from it casually, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it just said about רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may snack casually on fruit whose work is not finished. רבי אליעזר says that once תרומה is taken, the fruit becomes fixed, so even snacking is forbidden. The חכמים disagree, which shows this is a minority view.

keyTerms.meaning: Their processing work is finished
Casual eating, a snack
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: Fruits from which one took teruma
before their work was finished,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר לֶאֱכוֹל מֵהֶן עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer forbids eating from them casually,
and the Sages permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: פֵּירוֹת שֶׁתְּרָמָן עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב שימי בר אשי's claim about רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds תרומה fixes produce
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about fruit from which תרומה was taken before its work was finished

steps.title: A proof from the חכמים that שבת fixes produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second half of the משנה. It reasons that the חכמים allow the fruit only in שביעית, so in other years שבת must fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the second half: The חכמים say he must mark the fruit and say 'from here to there.' The reason it works is that it is ערב שבת in שביעית, when there is no tithing. But in the other years, when tithing applies, the fruit is forbidden. Why? Is it not because שבת fixes it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof, this time from the חכמים, that שבת fixes produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks about שביעית, when there are no מעשרות. The גמרא infers that in a regular year the fruit would be forbidden. It suggests the only reason is that שבת fixes it. Since this would be the view of the חכמים, it would settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
The second half of a משנה
The seventh year, when no מעשרות are taken
Subject to tithing
He marks the fruit

phrases.english: Come and hear from the second half of the mishna,
and the Sages say:
not until he marks it and says, 'from here to there.'
The reason is that it is Shabbat eve in the Sabbatical Year —
which is not subject to tithing,
but in the other years of the seven-year cycle,
which are subject to tithing — they are forbidden.
What is the reason?
Is it not because Shabbat fixes it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי אליעזר alone cannot settle the question, the גמרא tries to prove it from the חכמים
steps.raayaObject: That שבת fixes produce for מעשרות
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the חכמים's ruling in the second half of the משנה

steps.title: No, his own words fixed the fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The fruit is fixed because the person said 'from here to there I will eat tomorrow,' and not because of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, that case is different. Since he said 'from here to there I will eat tomorrow,' he fixed the fruit himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof. It gives a different reason the fruit would be forbidden in a regular year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed שבת is what fixes the fruit. But the person clearly set aside exactly which fruit he would eat as a meal, and that act fixes it. So the משנה does not show that שבת fixes produce.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different
He fixed it himself

phrases.english: No, there it is different,
since he said:
'From here to there I will eat tomorrow' —
he has fixed it.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fruit is fixed by the person's own declaration, not by שבת

steps.title: Then why mention שבת at all?
steps.stepSummary: If his declaration is what fixes the fruit, the same would be true on a weekday. So why does the משנה speak about שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why mention שבת? Even on a weekday it would be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just gave. If שבת plays no role, the משנה should not need to mention it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the declaration alone fixes the fruit, then שבת adds nothing. The משנה's focus on ערב שבת then looks unnecessary. The גמרא now needs a reason the משנה speaks about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically mention this?
A weekday

phrases.english: If so, why specifically Shabbat?
Even on a weekday it would be so too!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the declaration, not שבת, fixes the fruit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the משנה would have no reason to mention שבת

steps.title: טבל counts as prepared for שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions שבת to teach that טבל is considered prepared for שבת. If someone wrongly tithed it on שבת, the tithing works.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that טבל counts as prepared for שבת. If a person did wrong and tithed it on שבת, it is tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the משנה speaks about שבת. It closes this back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think untithed produce is מוקצה on שבת, since one may not tithe on שבת. The משנה teaches that it is still considered prepared for שבת. So if someone tithed it anyway, the fruit is fixed up and may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required portions have not yet been taken
Prepared, ready for use on שבת
He fixed it up by tithing it
This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The proof that שבת fixes produce was rejected, because the person's own declaration fixed it. The משנה still mentions שבת to teach that טבל is prepared for שבת: if it was wrongly tithed on שבת, it is tithed.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean you may tithe on שבת. It only means that if someone already did, the result counts.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that untithed produce is prepared with regard to Shabbat,
so that if he went ahead wrongly and tithed it, it is tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּטֶבֶל מוּכָן הוּא אֵצֶל שַׁבָּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining what the wording comes to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning שבת would be pointless if the declaration fixes the fruit
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת is mentioned to teach that טבל is prepared for שבת, so tithing it after the fact works

steps.title: A contradiction from the case of eating a cluster of grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets a source against our משנה. There, רבי אליעזר lets a person finish eating grapes even after he enters a חצר or שבת begins, which suggests שבת does not fix the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we raise a contradiction: If someone was eating from a cluster of grapes and walked from a garden into a courtyard, רבי אליעזר says he may finish and רבי יהושע says he may not. If it got dark on Friday night, רבי אליעזר says he may finish and רבי יהושע says he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different source that seems to clash with what we learned from our משנה about שבת fixing fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes still meant for pressing are not finished, and in a garden a person may snack on them without tithing. רבי אליעזר says he may 'finish' even after entering a חצר or when שבת starts. That sounds like neither חצר nor שבת fixes the fruit for רבי אליעזר, but our משנה seemed to show that שבת does fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And we set them against each other': the גמרא is raising a contradiction between two sources
A cluster of grapes
A courtyard; bringing fruit into it can make it 'fixed' for tithing
He may finish eating
It got dark on Friday night, so שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this source's רבי יהושע with the חכמים of our משנה. The clash here is about what רבי אליעזר himself holds.

phrases.english: And we raise a contradiction:
If one was eating from a cluster of grapes,
and he came in from a garden to a courtyard,
Rabbi Eliezer says: He may finish,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not finish.
If it grew dark on the night of Shabbat,
Rabbi Eliezer says: He may finish,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not finish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב שימי בר אשי's answer in step 7, that for רבי אליעזר שבת fixes produce, and challenges it from a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר lets a person finish eating once שבת begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's claim (step 7) that רבי אליעזר holds שבת fixes produce for tithing, all the more so than תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר lets a person finish eating grapes when שבת begins, then for him שבת does not fix the fruit. That contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: רבי נתן explains what 'he may finish' really means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this source gives its own explanation. רבי נתן says 'finish' means only after leaving the חצר or after שבת ends, so רבי אליעזר agrees that חצר and שבת do fix the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is as it is taught: רבי נתן says, when רבי אליעזר said 'he may finish,' he did not mean in the courtyard, but that he may go outside the courtyard and finish. And he did not mean on שבת, but that he waits until after שבת and finishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by quoting רבי נתן, who explains what רבי אליעזר meant by 'he may finish.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'finish' sounded like 'finish right now, without tithing.' רבי נתן says it means 'finish later': once he leaves the חצר, or once שבת is over. So even for רבי אליעזר, while he is in the חצר or on שבת the fruit counts as fixed, and there is no clash with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that other source
As the reason is taught; the source explains itself
He goes outside the courtyard
After שבת ends, Saturday night

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a short word like 'finish' can hide a time limit. Reading רבי אליעזר correctly removes the contradiction.

phrases.english: There, it is as the reason is taught,
phrases.notes: He means that this source itself spells out what רבי אליעזר meant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
Not that when Rabbi Eliezer said 'he may finish' —
he meant he may finish in the courtyard,
but rather: he goes outside the courtyard and finishes.
And not that when Rabbi Eliezer said 'he may finish' —
he meant he may finish on Shabbat,
but rather he waits until after Shabbat and finishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the challenging source using an explanation found within it (רבי נתן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He may finish' means right away, in the חצר or on שבת, so neither fixes the fruit for רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He may finish' means only after leaving the חצר or after שבת, so both do fix the fruit even for רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule: things fix fruit only when its work is finished
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that שבת, תרומה, חצר and buying all make fruit fixed for tithing only if its work is already finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: Whether שבת, or תרומה, or a courtyard, or a purchase, none of them fix the fruit except for things whose work is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the practical ruling, reported by רבין in the name of רבי יוחנן, about when fruit becomes fixed for tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוגיא discussed several things that can fix fruit: שבת, taking תרומה, bringing it into a חצר, and buying it. רבי יוחנן gives one rule for all four. None of them fixes fruit whose work is not yet finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether this or that; all are treated the same
A purchase, buying the fruit
They make the fruit 'fixed', so it must be tithed before eating
Their work is finished; the produce is fully processed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח all fix fruit for tithing only once its work is finished. Before that, they do not obligate tithing.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Whether Shabbat, or teruma,
or a courtyard, or a purchase —
none of them fix the fruit,
except for items whose work is finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradiction is resolved, the גמרא gives the final rule about what fixes fruit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שבת, תרומה, חצר and מקח fix produce for tithing only when its work is finished.

steps.title: Why שבת is in the list: to reject הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן listed שבת to exclude the opinion of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'שבת' in רבי יוחנן's rule is there to reject the opinion of הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining each item in רבי יוחנן's list, starting with שבת. It says that item is there to reject הלל's view, and it is setting up the source for that view in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said שבת fixes fruit for tithing only when its work is finished. That 'only when' is the new point. It means someone disagrees and holds that שבת fixes fruit even when its work is not finished, and the גמרא names that someone: הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude, to reject (a different opinion)
הלל הזקן, the great early sage

phrases.english: Shabbat —
phrases.notes: This is the first item in רבי יוחנן's list from the previous step. Now the גמרא explains why it is there.

phrases.english: comes to exclude the view of Hillel,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the purpose of each item in רבי יוחנן's list from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת is listed with the condition 'only if the work is finished' in order to reject הלל, who holds otherwise.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing הלל's view on fruit still being worked on when שבת begins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if someone was gathering fruit to process it and שבת began, רבי יהודה reports that הלל alone forbids eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone was gathering fruit from place to place to finish working on it, and שבת began while it was still unfinished, רבי יהודה said that הלל, on his own, forbids eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows where הלל's opinion comes from. This is the view that רבי יוחנן's rule rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the fruit's work is not finished, yet הלל still forbids eating it without tithing. That means הלל holds that the start of שבת fixes the fruit even before its work is done. רבי יוחנן, by adding 'only if its work is finished,' disagrees with הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
one who gathers or piles up (fruit)
and the day became holy over them, meaning שבת began
forbids

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: שבת fixes fruit for tithing only if its work is finished. הלל (alone) holds that שבת fixes it even if the work is not finished.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הלל לעצמו' as 'forbids it for himself only.' Here it means הלל is the only one who forbids it.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One who gathers fruits from place to place
in order to reap them,
and the day became holy upon them,
phrases.notes: In other words, שבת started while the fruit was still in this unfinished state.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Hillel, on his own, forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַמְעַמֵּר פֵּירוֹת מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם לִקְצוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the view of הלל that step 16 said is being excluded.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion (הלל) that שבת fixes fruit for tithing even before its work is finished.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה reports that הלל alone forbids eating fruit that was still being gathered for processing when שבת began.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוחנן's condition 'only if its work is finished' is a real position. It decides a disagreement and rejects הלל's stricter view.
